title: The Ground Where Rice Once Grew
subtitle: 竞技体育 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 竞技体育（文学艺术与体育·竞技体育与赛事）
meta: 主题语境：竞技体育（文学艺术与体育·竞技体育与赛事）　|　核心词汇：field　|　正文 374 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 field 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: Our school's running track was once a rice ① field. The old men in the village still call it the paddy, and my father's generation remember harvesting there in October. Nobody alive remembers who decided it should become a sports ground, and every April we line up on it as though that were the natural order of things. Sports fields, I suppose, always look permanent to the people standing on them.

My own part in this was small. I was never going to win anything, so I learned to do something else: ② to field questions for the teachers at registration, and later ③ to field the ball in rounders, because nobody else wanted that corner of the playground. Standing there, I noticed that a match is mostly waiting, and that waiting has a shape of its own.

In my second year a new PE teacher arrived who had once run abroad. On her first afternoon she made us sit down and count the competitors: seven events, sixty-one of them, and one ④ field of eleven runners in the eight hundred metres, six of whom had trained all winter. 'You cannot beat the whole field,' she said. 'You can beat the version of you that arrived last September.'

She also took us beyond sport. Once a month she drove four of us out of town on a ⑤ field trip — to a river, a hill, a weather station — and made us measure things: speed, depth, temperature, patience. I began to suspect that my own ⑥ field of interest was something quieter than running. I liked the numbers, the waiting, the slow accumulation of evidence.

That spring our school ⑦ fielded its first girls' relay team. They trained on the same ⑧ field where the rice had once grown, at six in the morning, with the dew still on it. On the day of the meeting they came second, and the whole ⑨ field — winners included — stood at the line to watch them finish. My grandmother, who had harvested that ground as a girl, walked slowly across the ⑩ field afterwards and touched the grass, then looked up at the scoreboard for a very long time. Some fields feed you and some fields measure you; this one used to do both.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: C. n. 领域；专业范围
D. n. （比赛的）全体参赛者；场上选手
F. v. 处理；应付（问题、提问）
G. v. 派（队）上场；让……参赛
H. 固定搭配：field trip 实地考察；野外考察

items.q: to field questions for the teachers
to field the ball in rounders
out of town on a field trip
our school fielded its first girls' relay team
the same field where the rice had once grown
walked slowly across the field afterwards

answers.why: a rice field 与后面的 harvesting、October 呼应，是名词“稻田、田地”。
field＋questions，是动词“应付、处理（提问）”，指在报名处替老师回答问题。
field the ball 是球类术语，意为“接球、守球”，与 rounders 这一运动相配。
a field of＋数量＋runners 指“全体参赛者”，与后文 beat the whole field 呼应。
on a field trip 是固定搭配，意为“实地考察”，后文的 river、hill、weather station 正是考察地点。
field of interest 意为“感兴趣的领域”，是抽象义“领域、专业范围”。
field＋队伍，是动词“派（队）参赛”，指首次派出女子接力队。
the same field where rice had once grown 指同一块场地，此处已作运动场用。
the whole field 与第 4 题同义，指场上全部参赛者，连获胜者也停下来看。
across the field 指穿过这块场地，祖母年轻时正是在这里收割。

answers: Our school's running track was once a rice field.
At registration I fielded questions for the teachers.
In baseball, fielding the ball is a basic skill.
Last month our school fielded a girls' relay team.
Every month she takes four students on a field trip.
I have found my own field of interest at last.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 field 的 3 种不同用法；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: The running track behind our school was once a rice field, and the old men still call it the paddy.
I was never going to win a race, so I fielded questions instead, and later learned to field the ball.
Of the sixty-one competitors, one field of eleven had trained all winter for the eight hundred metres.
Once a month our teacher took us on a field trip, and that was how I found my own field of interest.
That spring our school fielded its first girls' relay team, and they trained on the same field at six each morning.
On the day of the meeting the whole field stopped to watch them finish, and afterwards my grandmother walked slowly across the wet ground.
